quotes.text: enable **Reusable payment methods for Global Payouts**.
Stripe handles the display of eligible payment methods using [dynamic payment methods]
We’ll send you an email confirmation no later than 5 days after your confirmation of this Direct Debit Authority.
Notification of success or failure of the PaymentIntent comes within 3 business days after Stripe submits the debit.
When you use a target date, the PaymentIntent’s status transitions to `processing` as soon as you confirm the PaymentIntent.

findings: November adds practical Accounts v2 preview entry guidance (Account previews and features → Reusable payment methods for Global Payouts) and a 2026-10-28.preview header on its Account creation example. The May preview request line was incomplete and its Node.js Account example lacked that explicit version (old raw lines 25–56; new raw lines 31–65). Connect general availability and non-Connect public preview remain scoped statements about the Accounts v2 API, separate from NZ BECS payment-method approval.

November switches the documented initial and reuse configurations from explicit nz_bank_account in payment_method_types to Dashboard enablement with dynamic eligible-method display and automatic_payment_methods[enabled]=true in examples. It adds an Accounts v2 customer_account version of the off-session example alongside the Customers v1 customer version. The saved-method attachment condition remains successful initial PaymentIntent with setup_future_usage=off_session (old raw lines 71–109 and 319–337; new raw lines 76–106 and 291–321).

November authority sample says no later than five days, while the May sample said five business days. The existing mandate acknowledgement, proof on request, default Stripe emails and day-of-debit deadline remain, and November clarifies that the three-business-day success/failure notification interval begins when Stripe submits the debit (old raw lines 240–257 and 295–317; new raw lines 215–232 and 269–289).

November adds the scheduled debit's confirmation-to-processing and subsequent bank settlement/rejection states, plus the associated Charge payment_method_details.expected_debit_date through charge.updated. The May guide already documented the best-effort target window, cancellation cutoff and rolling-date conditions (old raw lines 371–382; new raw lines 355–368). The product overview separately confirms this Charge field is an estimate (raw/stripe-payments-nz-bank-account-2026-11-07.md lines 210–222).

Mapped source lines 19 and 30–38 summarize May’s explicit list and Customers v1 reuse. They need date and path qualifiers and the November dynamic enablement, automatic methods examples, both customer identities on reuse, and Accounts v2 preview scope (old raw lines 25–109 and 319–337; new raw lines 31–106 and 291–321).

Mapped source lines 21–26 omit separate terms display and confirmed acceptance outside Payment Element, requested mandate-record retention/provision, mandate and debit emails, and the distinction between processing and verified completion for fulfillment. Add the five-day November sample and dated conflict warning. Relevant authority is old raw lines 238–257 and 293–317 and new raw lines 213–232 and 241–289.

Mapped source line 43 omits the existing roll-forward condition when fewer than three business days ahead and omits the November Charge expected_debit_date and explicit scheduled-state sequence. Compare old raw lines 371–382 with new raw lines 355–368. Source line 54’s ‘indefinitely’ should be qualified to the sandbox entry remaining processing absent a separate API transition, as both versions describe (old raw lines 349–369; new raw lines 323–353). Neither pinned excerpt supplies that transition’s API request.

Node.js install and server/intent examples gave way to Ruby setup and client-secret examples and cURL account/PaymentIntent examples; Stripe.js sample changed Dahlia to Endive, quote/table formatting changed, and the appearance screenshot uses a CDN link. These preserve dated example context but do not establish SDK deprecation, a mandatory language migration or a November-only runtime contract (old raw lines 12–23, 41–69, 111–203 and 259–264; new raw lines 13–29, 47–74, 108–180 and 234–239).

Mapped source lines 19–23 omit the browser prerequisite and compress confirmation into an unconditional processing arrow. Both captures require loading Stripe.js directly from js.stripe.com and initializing it with the client publishable key (old raw lines 184–203, new raw lines 161–180). For NZ BECS alone, stripe.confirmPayment may use redirect='if_required' and omit return_url. Add return_url when including a redirect-based method in the dynamic integration (old raw lines 266–293, new raw lines 241–267). The client handles errors and requires_payment_method, with processing after successful submission. Fulfill only after verifying success independently of client submission. Stripe recommends webhooks and provides Dashboard event visibility (new raw lines 275–289).

The NZ BECS concept at wiki/concepts/stripe-nz-becs-debit.md line 74 currently presents payment_method_types: ['nz_bank_account'] without a date. Scope that step to the May guide (old raw lines 71–109), add the distinct Dashboard-enabled dynamic route shown in November (new raw lines 76–106), and link from the acceptance summary back to the concept, whose reciprocal acceptance entry is at line 83.

conflicts: The dated May acceptance and setup guide samples say five business days (old raw lines 246–255 and raw/stripe-nz-becs-set-up-payment-2025.md lines 200–212), while the May product overview already says five days (raw/stripe-nz-becs-debit-2025.md lines 135–143). November acceptance lines 221–230, setup sample (raw/stripe-payments-nz-bank-account-set-up-payment-2026-11-07.md lines 211–224), and product overview (raw/stripe-payments-nz-bank-account-2026-11-07.md lines 224–249) all say five days. Date the May sample discrepancy in the acceptance source and route reciprocally through the NZ BECS overview/setup sources and concept. The mandate email follows successful confirmation and is separate from the required notice of date and amount no later than each debit day. The concept and overview summary describe send timing tied to confirmation (wiki/concepts/stripe-nz-becs-debit.md lines 30–36 and wiki/sources/source-stripe-nz-becs-debit.md lines 23–27); the overview’s default immediate send following successful confirmation and the latest allowed day of debit should be distinguished.

The November acceptance guide explicitly illustrates off_session=true reuse for both account models (new raw lines 291–321), while the contemporaneous product overview APIs table marks Off-session payments unsupported at raw/stripe-payments-nz-bank-account-2026-11-07.md lines 191–196 even as it marks Payment Intents with setup_future_usage and Setup Intents supported. Preserve the conflict visibly and reciprocally on the acceptance and overview sources, in the NZ BECS concept and when routing its save-for-future guide (wiki/sources/source-stripe-nz-becs-set-up-payment.md lines 13–33). Neither archived example nor generic API row establishes the effective account, integration or product eligibility or resolves the conflict. The overview’s integration link label also calls this ‘Manually configure’ (lines 197–207), although the November guide body documents dynamic selection. Use the link label as navigation rather than overriding the body.

Do not conflate notification latency in the acceptance guide (within three business days after Stripe submits the debit, new raw lines 275–289) with the overview’s standard payment-success and funds-available T+2 table (raw/stripe-payments-nz-bank-account-2026-11-07.md lines 210–222). The May overview introduction describes success/failure notification as taking up to two business days after initiation (raw/stripe-nz-becs-debit-2025.md lines 1–12), while the May acceptance guide said within three business days 'thereafter' (old raw lines 303–317). Keep the dated bases visible if comparing the claims, and distinguish initiation, debit submission, notification, and settlement.

Its effective scope and the supported account or integration paths remain unresolved given the acceptance guide's off-session examples (new raw lines 291–321).

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/nz-bank-account/accept-a-payment, November documents NZD web Elements acceptance through a server-created PaymentIntent, a customer-configured Account using customer_account or a Customers v1 object using customer, Dashboard enablement and dynamic display of eligible methods (new raw lines 13-15 and 31-108). The separate November overview adds NZ eligibility, approval and verification requirements (raw/stripe-payments-nz-bank-account-2026-11-07.md lines 9-27). The guide’s Accounts v2 note describes Connect general availability, public preview for other Stripe users and the preview feature/version steps (new raw lines 35-65). The browser loads Stripe.js directly from js.stripe.com, initializes Stripe with the client publishable key, and uses the Intent's client secret to collect details and accept Direct Debit Authority terms in Payment Element (old raw lines 184-203; new raw lines 161-180 and 195-232). A custom UI must display the terms and confirm acceptance itself, and mandate records must be supplied on request (new raw lines 195-232). For NZ BECS alone, stripe.confirmPayment can use redirect='if_required' and omit return_url. A redirect-based method added to the dynamic integration requires return_url (old raw lines 266-293; new raw lines 241-267). The sample handles errors and requires_payment_method. Successful submission enters processing, and fulfillment waits for independently verified success. Stripe recommends using webhooks, such as payment_intent.succeeded, and also shows the events in Dashboard (new raw lines 275-289). Send mandate confirmation after successful confirmation and give the date and amount of each debit by debit day, with Stripe sending by default (new raw lines 241-289). The guide illustrates reuse of the attached PaymentMethod after the original PaymentIntent succeeds with setup_future_usage=off_session and adds scheduled debit statuses and associated Charge tracking (new raw lines 291-321 and 355-368). The separate overview contradicts the off-session examples. The May capture shows explicit nz_bank_account lists, a v1-only reuse example and the same delayed-outcome framework (old raw lines 71-109 and 266-337). source-stripe-nz-becs-accept-payment.md retains that core flow but needs these dated prerequisites, notification and target-date distinctions.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/nz-bank-account/accept-a-payment, the substantive guidance changes are Dashboard enablement with dynamic methods and automatic-payment-method examples, a concrete Accounts v2 preview opt-in and preview-version example, and a new customer_account replay example alongside the v1 customer path (old raw lines 25-109 and 319-337; new raw lines 31-106 and 291-321). Retain the May explicit method-list examples as dated in both the acceptance summary and the NZ BECS concept, whose line 74 currently presents that list without qualification. Link the acceptance summary back to the concept and keep the November dynamic route visible. Ruby/cURL versus Node.js, Endive versus Dahlia Stripe.js samples and the appearance/table formatting are dated presentation and version context without deprecation evidence. The custom mandate sample changes five business days to five days (old raw lines 246-257; new raw lines 215-232), aligning with the separately captured May and November overview wording. Keep that discrepancy visible via reciprocal acceptance, overview and setup routes. The separate November overview’s APIs table marks Off-session payments unsupported (raw/stripe-payments-nz-bank-account-2026-11-07.md lines 191-196), while the acceptance guide documents off_session=true for both identities. Warn reciprocally and retain the unresolved scope. Stripe's default send timing and merchant notice deadline are separate from the three-business-day status notification measured after debit submission (new raw lines 269-289). The target selection window remains 3–15 days from the current date, and cancellation is available up to three business days before the configured date. A target on a non-business day or fewer than three business days away rolls forward to the next available business day. The target date is best effort. November adds processing on confirmation, success after bank settlement or requires_payment_method after rejection and expected_debit_date through charge.updated on the associated Charge (old raw lines 371-382; new raw lines 355-368). In source-stripe-nz-becs-accept-payment.md, retain that estimate as distinct from settlement and fulfillment, and keep sandbox outcomes separate from actual payments.
